chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan who said:

A group of our companions performed Hajj, and when they arrived in Madinah, they visited Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). They said, 'Zurarah commanded us to commence our Hajj with Talbiyah when we entered the state of Ihram.' He (the Imam) said to them, 'Perform Hajj al-Tamattu'.' When they left from his presence, I entered upon him and said, 'May I be your ransom, if you do not inform them of what you informed Zurarah, we will surely go to Kufah and make him a liar.' He said, 'Call them back.' So they entered upon him, and he said, 'Zurarah has spoken the truth.' Then he said, 'By Allah, no one will hear this from me after this day.'

key_terms.أَحْرَمْنَا: We entered the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعُوا: Perform Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.زُرَارَةَ: Zurarah ibn A'yan (a prominent companion of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Hajj al-Tamattu' according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) in this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of *taqiyya* (strategic dissimulation) in Shia jurisprudence, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) initially advised Hajj al-Tamattu' to his companions to align with the prevailing Sunni practice and avoid political suspicion. Upon the narrator's request for consistency with the ruling given to Zurarah, the Imam confirmed the validity of Tamattu' but declared it would not be repeated for others, signaling a shift in communal practice or a specific contextual ruling to be kept confidential.
